structured_output.text: Not proved. I believe the answer is yes (recalled from the literature, not derived here). Heuristic: a random set with Pr(n in A)=sqrt(c log n / n) has E[1_A*1_A(n)] ~ pi c log n, since the sum of 1/sqrt(a(n-a)) over a<n tends to pi. But Chernoff deviations of relative size eps occur with probability about n^{-pi c eps^2/2}, which is not summable for small eps, so Borel-Cantelli fails and a plain random construction gives no limit. A construction that suppresses these fluctuations (deterministic, or random plus a correction step) is missing and I did not carry one out.
